summary: Aermotor lookout erected in 1936 after an earlier wooden tower; the NHLR says it remains in service, and a 2018 camp field trip is the latest visit evidence found.

facts.design: 100-ft Aermotor tower with a 7x7-ft steel cab (1936)

events.note: Original wooden tower. The NHLR gives 1927 as fact; the Forest Lookouts list marks it with a question mark.
55-ft steel tower maintained by the Oklahoma Forest Service; 2,100 people from 20 states and Canada registered there during 1929.
Buddy Baker worked as a watchman on Carter Mountain for four years; the start year is not given.
In June 1930 Baker spotted smoke about two miles from the tower and put out flames while a sleeping three-year-old's bedding was only starting to smoke.
A 100-ft Aermotor tower with a 7x7 steel cab. The NHLR says it replaced the original wooden tower; the Forest Lookouts list says it was erected.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, September 16, 1997.
A state press release dated 03.27.2018 lists field trips to the Carter Mountain Fire Tower as part of a teen forestry camp.

corrections.why: Both sources describe the 1936 structure as a 100-foot Aermotor tower. 16.8 m is about 55 ft, which matches the 1929 steel tower the 1930 newspaper describes, not the 1936 tower that stands today.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NHLR says the 1936 Aermotor replaced the original wooden tower. The 1930 newspaper quoted by the Forest Lookouts site describes a 55-foot steel tower already in use in 1929. The record keeps both; the order between 1927 and 1936 is unclear.
The NHLR states 1927 as fact; the Forest Lookouts site marks the wooden tower's date with a question mark.

notes_for_editor: No access level or visit rules were found, so access is left out of facts. The NHLR's 'remains in service' has no date and is the only current-status source. The 2018 press release is the latest visit evidence. LASR (403) and a Facebook post (login wall) could not be read. The height correction (16.8 m to 30.5 m) is the main change to the record; check the 100-ft figure against the tower if measured data exists. Staffing today was not found.
